question: Which of the following is responsible for the red colour of beetroot?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Betanin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Betanin is a red pigment found in beetroots and is responsible for their characteristic color.

• It belongs to the class of betalains, which are water-soluble pigments.

• Betanin is used as a natural food colorant and has the E number E162.

• In addition to its coloring properties, betanin also exhibits antioxidant properties, which can provide health benefits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Curcumin**

• Curcumin is a bright yellow chemical produced by some plants, mainly turmeric.

• It is used as a dietary supplement, in cosmetics, as a food coloring, and as flavoring in food.

• It has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties and is being studied for its potential health benefits.

• **Beta Carotene**

• Beta carotene is a red-orange pigment found in plants and fruits, especially carrots and colorful vegetables.

• It is a precursor of vitamin A, which is essential for vision, immune function, and skin health.

• Beta carotene is also an antioxidant, which helps protect cells from damage.

• **Lycopene**

• Lycopene is a bright red carotenoid hydrocarbon found in tomatoes and other red fruits and vegetables.

• It has antioxidant properties and may help prevent certain diseases, including heart disease and cancer.

• Lycopene is used as a food coloring and is also available as a dietary supplement.
